questions.question: In the RLHF pipeline, why are pairwise preferences generally favored over absolute scalar ratings during human data collection?
questions.choice_A: They reduce annotator calibration burden and yield more consistent comparative judgments across annotators
questions.choice_B: They require fewer annotations to achieve the same statistical power as ratings
questions.choice_C: They allow direct optimization of policy parameters without a reward model
questions.choice_D: They eliminate the need for quality control protocols in annotation

questions.question: When constructing a reward model from preference data, what is the typical objective used to train the model on pairwise comparisons?
questions.choice_A: Mean squared error between predicted and true scalar rewards
questions.choice_B: A logistic likelihood that the preferred sample has higher cumulative reward than the dispreferred one
questions.choice_C: Hinge loss over the difference in token-level log-probabilities
questions.choice_D: KL divergence between the policy and the reference model

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the standard three-stage RLHF pipeline?
questions.choice_A: Collect preferences → train policy with PPO from scratch → distill to a supervised model
questions.choice_B: Train reward model → pretrain language model → collect human ratings
questions.choice_C: Supervised fine-tuning on demonstrations → reward modeling from preferences → RL fine-tuning guided by the reward
questions.choice_D: Inverse RL to infer dynamics → behavior cloning → off-policy evaluation

questions.question: In reward modeling for RLHF, why is a partition function sometimes introduced when defining a preference likelihood?
questions.choice_A: To normalize the policy’s output probabilities across tokens
questions.choice_B: To enforce a baseline that centers the rewards at zero
questions.choice_C: To guarantee convexity of the optimization problem
questions.choice_D: To ensure the pairwise probability distribution over outcomes is properly normalized

questions.question: What is a practical reason to start RLHF from an SFT-initialized policy rather than from a pretrained model without instruction tuning?
questions.choice_A: SFT reduces exploration burden by placing the policy near human-preferred regions of the response space
questions.choice_B: SFT eliminates the need for reward normalization during RL
questions.choice_C: SFT guarantees on-policy data collection is unnecessary
questions.choice_D: SFT ensures exact optimality of the final policy under the reward model

questions.question: In PPO as used in RLHF, what is the purpose of the clipping objective on the probability ratio between new and old policies?
questions.choice_A: To exactly enforce a trust-region constraint in parameter space
questions.choice_B: To limit the size of policy updates and stabilize training by preventing large changes where the advantage is positive or negative
questions.choice_C: To normalize the reward scale per episode
questions.choice_D: To reduce variance in gradient estimates by subtracting a baseline

questions.question: Why is a KL penalty to a reference model often added during RL fine-tuning in RLHF?
questions.choice_A: To force the model to match ground-truth labels exactly
questions.choice_B: To increase the entropy of the policy irrespective of the reward
questions.choice_C: To regularize against distribution drift and preserve helpful behaviors learned during SFT
questions.choice_D: To correct for off-policy bias introduced by replay buffers

questions.question: Which annotation protocol choice is most likely to improve inter-rater reliability in pairwise preference collection?
questions.choice_A: Allowing annotators to freely redefine the task guidelines mid-session
questions.choice_B: Using majority vote only, without qualification tests
questions.choice_C: Presenting unbalanced pair lengths to increase contrast between options
questions.choice_D: Providing clear rubrics, calibration examples, and periodic gold-standard checks

questions.question: What is the role of baselines in policy gradient methods like REINFORCE within RLHF?
questions.choice_A: They reduce variance by centering the returns or rewards used to compute advantages
questions.choice_B: They convert on-policy sampling into off-policy learning
questions.choice_C: They ensure the gradient estimate is unbiased only if the baseline depends on actions
questions.choice_D: They are used exclusively to normalize token-level log-probabilities

questions.question: A common architecture for the reward model in language RLHF is:
questions.choice_A: A convolutional network over token embeddings with a scalar head per token
questions.choice_B: The same transformer backbone as the policy, with a scalar reward head that scores full sequences
questions.choice_C: A separate RNN that predicts per-token value functions
questions.choice_D: A diffusion model scoring prefix-noise trajectories

questions.question: Which challenge is most directly linked to the reward model over-optimizing on idiosyncrasies of the collected preferences, leading to degraded real-world behavior?
questions.choice_A: Sparse rewards
questions.choice_B: Credit assignment
questions.choice_C: Reward hacking and overoptimization
questions.choice_D: Partial observability

questions.question: In practice, why might one normalize rewards during RL fine-tuning after switching or updating the reward model?
questions.choice_A: To preserve exact equivalence to maximum likelihood training
questions.choice_B: To guarantee the KL penalty can be removed
questions.choice_C: To enable off-policy importance sampling without variance
questions.choice_D: To stabilize training by keeping advantage scales consistent across updates

questions.question: Which statement best characterizes sample efficiency concerns in RLHF?
questions.choice_A: Preference data collection is costly, so active selection of prompts and pairs can yield better learning per human label
questions.choice_B: On-policy data is unnecessary because reward models perfectly generalize
questions.choice_C: PPO always guarantees optimal sample efficiency given any reward model
questions.choice_D: Annotator disagreement implies the data is unusable for learning

questions.question: What is a common empirical practice when training the reward model on pairwise data to avoid degenerate solutions?
questions.choice_A: Forcing the reward head to predict token-level log-likelihoods directly
questions.choice_B: Regularizing the reward magnitude (e.g., via weight decay or explicit variance control) and monitoring the implied Bradley–Terry temperature
questions.choice_C: Training the policy and reward model jointly from scratch to convergence
questions.choice_D: Removing the preference likelihood and using mean squared error on arbitrary targets

questions.question: During RL fine-tuning, why is an advantage estimator used instead of raw rewards?
questions.choice_A: Advantages introduce bias that accelerates policy improvement
questions.choice_B: Advantages remove any need for a value function
questions.choice_C: Advantages center returns relative to a baseline, reducing variance while preserving unbiased gradients
questions.choice_D: Advantages make the optimization convex in policy parameters

questions.question: How does distribution mismatch manifest in the RLHF pipeline?
questions.choice_A: The reward model is trained on the same distribution as it evaluates during RL, ensuring no mismatch
questions.choice_B: The policy is trained on synthetic data while the reward model is trained on human speech audio
questions.choice_C: The SFT policy’s outputs perfectly match the pretrained model’s outputs
questions.choice_D: The reward model is trained on preference data from an earlier policy but must score samples from a later, shifted policy during RL

questions.question: Which of the following best describes REINFORCE in the RLHF setting?
questions.choice_A: A Monte Carlo policy gradient method using log-probability gradients weighted by returns or advantages
questions.choice_B: A second-order optimization method that inverts the Fisher information matrix
questions.choice_C: A deterministic policy gradient method tailored for continuous control
questions.choice_D: An off-policy actor-critic algorithm using Q-learning targets

questions.question: What is a practical mitigation for instability when the policy begins to exploit imperfections in the reward model?
questions.choice_A: Remove the KL penalty to encourage faster exploration
questions.choice_B: Use early stopping and refresh the reward model with new preference data drawn from the current policy’s outputs
questions.choice_C: Freeze the policy and increase learning rates for the reward model indefinitely
questions.choice_D: Switch to pure supervised fine-tuning without any human feedback

questions.question: Why is it common to mix prompts or trajectories from a reference policy during RLHF fine-tuning?
questions.choice_A: To ensure the optimization objective becomes convex
questions.choice_B: To avoid evaluating the reward model on any on-policy data
questions.choice_C: To regularize learning and prevent catastrophic drift by anchoring to known-good behavior
questions.choice_D: To remove the need for value baselines and advantage estimation

questions.question: In pairwise preference training, what does the Bradley–Terry model assume about the probability one item is preferred to another?
questions.choice_A: It equals the softmax over their absolute lengths
questions.choice_B: It is the sigmoid of a linear function of annotator features only
questions.choice_C: It is a logistic function of the difference in their latent scores produced by the reward model
questions.choice_D: It is uniform regardless of item quality

questions.question: Which challenge is most closely linked to the need for careful reward normalization and monitoring during training?
questions.choice_A: Exploration in continuous action spaces
questions.choice_B: Sensitivity of policy updates to reward scale, which can destabilize PPO or advantage estimation
questions.choice_C: The impossibility of estimating advantages without a model of the environment
questions.choice_D: The requirement that the partition function be computed exactly at every step
